Non-field `function` patterns (methods, constructors, operators, indexers) are unaffected because `CSharpPropertyHeaderPrefixRegex` requires the line to end before `(` or `{`. Added a seventh regression test `Extract_CSharp_PlainField_FreeModifierOrder` covering `static public int X;`, `readonly public int Y;`, `new public static int Z = 1;`, the multi-line generic field, and the multi-line const. The event row also previously rejected the inheritance modifiers that are legal on event declarations per the C# spec (`virtual` / `override` / `abstract` / `sealed`), and the interface and delegate rows did not accept the `file` file-scoped type modifier (or `new` for nested delegate hiding), so `abstract public event System.EventHandler E;`, `virtual public event System.EventHandler E;`, `sealed public override event System.EventHandler E;`, `file interface I {}`, and `file delegate int D(int x);` were dropped from symbol extraction. The plain-field negative lookahead was also too narrow: because `abstract` / `virtual` / `override` / `sealed` / `async` / `partial` / `file` / `ref` were not in the rejected-leading-token list, a declaration like `abstract public event System.EventHandler A;` was matching the plain-field row with `return_type` absorbing `"abstract public event System.EventHandler"` and `visibility` left empty. Added `virtual` / `override` / `abstract` / `sealed` / `new` to the event modifier alternation, added `file` / `new` to the interface and delegate alternations, and added `abstract` / `virtual` / `override` / `sealed` / `async` / `partial` / `file` / `ref` to the plain-field negative lookahead so non-field leading modifiers can no longer bleed into `return_type`. Added an eighth regression test `Extract_CSharp_InheritanceAndFile_FreeModifierOrder` pinning `file interface`, `file delegate`, and four inheritance-modifier event forms (`abstract public`, `virtual public`, `sealed public override`, `new public`) with `visibility="public"`. Updated the C# language-pattern row in `DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md` to note that modifier order is now accepted in any position. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/SymbolExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/SymbolExtractorTests.cs`, `DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`. Closes #355.
- **POSIX filenames containing `\` no longer become phantom `/` subdirectories in the index (#191)** — `FileIndexer.BuildRecordWithRawBytes` and several CLI helpers (`GitHelper.GetChangedFilesFromCommit`, `IndexCommandRunner` full-scan / `--commits` / `--files` path normalization and `.git/info/exclude` computation, `QueryCommandRunner.RunOutline`) unconditionally ran `Replace('\\', '/')` on relative paths regardless of the host OS. On Windows that is correct because `\` is the directory separator, but on POSIX `\` is a legal filename character (data-science notebooks with awkward names, generated / escaped paths, adversarial filenames) so a single-component file called `back\slash.py` was silently rewritten to `back/slash.py`. The file was then stored as if there were a `back/` directory containing `slash.py`, `excerpt 'back\slash.py'` and `outline back\slash.py` returned "No excerpt found" / null because the DB key was the mangled form, `files` / `map` / `outline` advertised a phantom `back/` subdirectory that does not exist on disk, and AI clients building mental maps from those outputs wasted tool calls exploring the imaginary directory. Added a single `FileIndexer.NormalizePathSeparators` helper that only runs the `\`→`/` conversion when `Path.DirectorySeparatorChar == '\\'` (i.e. on Windows), and replaced all nine storage and lookup sites so Windows indexes still normalize separators while POSIX indexes preserve `\` inside filenames verbatim. Internal pattern-matching helpers (`NormalizeIgnorePath` for gitignore rules, `NormalizeScopeKey` for ambiguous-project scope grouping) are intentionally left unchanged because they operate on gitignore-style patterns, not filesystem-literal paths. Added a POSIX-gated `BuildRecord_PreservesBackslashInPosixFilename` unit test that creates a `back\slash.py` file on disk and asserts `record.Path` is stored as `back\slash.py`, a `GetExcerptAndOutline_RoundTripPathContainingBackslash` DB-level regression that pins `excerpt` / `outline` lookups succeed against the literal path and fail against the mangled `back/slash.py` form, and cross-platform unit tests for `NormalizePathSeparators` itself covering both the Windows-separator and POSIX-no-op branches. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/FileIndexer.cs`, `src/CodeIndex/Cli/GitHelper.cs`, `src/CodeIndex/Cli/IndexCommandRunner.cs`, `src/CodeIndex/Cli/QueryCommandRunner.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/FileIndexerTests.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/DbReaderTests.cs`. Closes #191.
- **Multi-line C# enum members, JS/TS bare methods, and C# record primary-ctor headers no longer leak `\r` into signatures on CRLF sources (#405)** — `SymbolExtractor.GetSourceSpanText` (used to build C# enum member signatures via `TryAddCSharpEnumMemberFromSpan`), `TryCaptureJavaScriptTypeScriptMethodHeader` (used to build `Signature` for JS/TS class-body methods whose header wraps across physical lines), and `CollectRecordDeclarationText` (used internally to parse C# record primary-constructor components) all concatenated `lines[...]` slices with a literal `'\n'` separator without stripping the trailing `'\r'` that `content.Split('\n')` leaves on CRLF-terminated input. As a result, Windows / `autocrlf=true` / Visual Studio-saved sources produced signatures carrying OS-dependent `"\r\n"` between physical lines, breaking cross-OS signature equality, snapshot tests, and any downstream consumer that compared signatures by string equality. This is the same class of bug that `#382` fixed for `BuildCSharpTypeHeaderSignature`. All three paths now use a shared `StripTrailingCr` / `GetLineLengthExcludingTrailingCr` helper to drop one trailing `'\r'` per line before appending, so inter-line separators stay `'\n'` regardless of source line endings. For the JS/TS path, both the source builder and the sanitized builder strip in lockstep so the column-to-source mapping in `TryMapJavaScriptTypeScriptHeaderColumnToSourceLocation` stays aligned. Added three regression tests that construct CRLF-terminated content for each extractor path (a multi-line C# enum member span, a wrapped JS class-body method, and a wrapped C# record primary constructor) so the fix is pinned for every path. Bare-CR (old-Mac) line endings remain out of scope because `content.Split('\n')` does not split them at all. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/SymbolExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/SymbolExtractorTests.cs`. Closes #405.
- **Wrapped C# class / struct / interface / enum headers now preserve their base list and `where` clauses in `symbols.signature` (#382)** — `SymbolExtractor` previously sliced `SymbolRecord.Signature` for C# type declarations from the single physical line the declaration regex matched, so headers whose base list or generic constraints wrapped onto following lines — e.g. `public sealed class Foo<T>\n    : BaseFoo<T>, IBar, IBaz\n    where T : class, new()\n{` — truncated to `public sealed class Foo<T>` and silently lost every `:` base, interface, and `where T : ...` clause. Downstream consumers that read the signature to recover the base type (the planned `ParseCSharpBaseType` path in #257, future type-position reference extraction for #256, any lint or `impact` / `analyze_symbol` flow that wants to answer "what does this class extend?" from the index alone) degraded to "no base type" for every wrapped-header C# class on every large library that uses formatter-wrapped headers (ASP.NET Core, Roslyn, EF Core, xUnit, `Microsoft.Extensions.*`, etc.). The C# signature path now extends the existing multi-line-signature mechanism (already used for properties) to type declarations: a new `TryFindCSharpTypeHeaderExtent` helper scans forward from the header start using `LexCSharpLine` so `{` / `;` inside string literals, comments, and verbatim / raw strings are ignored, tracks paren depth (C# 12 primary constructor parameter lists) and bracket depth (attributes on type or generic parameters) so a nested `{` / `;` can never short-circuit the scan, terminates at the first body-opening `{` or primary-constructor / forward-declaration `;` at zero depth, and caps lookahead at 64 lines to stay safe on unterminated input. A dedicated `BuildCSharpTypeHeaderSignature` assembles the header slice by concatenating the relevant `[startColumn, endColumn)` span from each physical line with a literal `'\n'` between lines, then runs the combined text through a single-pass `SanitizeCSharpTypeHeaderSlice` that strips `//` line comments (terminated at the next `'\n'`) and `/* ... */` block comments, collapses runs of Code-mode whitespace (including the newlines between lines) into a single space, and preserves String / Verbatim / Raw / Char literal contents verbatim — including multi-line raw / verbatim strings, which keep every internal line break and leading indentation instead of being `Trim()`ed and space-joined. The sanitizer also tracks C# interpolation holes with an explicit frame stack: `$"..."`, `$@"..."`, `@$"..."`, `$"""..."""`, and `$$"""{{expr}}"""` each push a String / Verbatim / Raw frame marked `Interpolated`, and a hole opens only when the `{` run is at least as long as the number of `$` prefixes (with `{{` and `}}` still honored as literal-brace escapes in non-raw interpolated strings). Inside a hole, the sanitizer re-enters Code mode and matching nested braces before returning to the outer literal, so `$"{@"a  b"}  c"` now keeps the inner verbatim literal's double-space intact and the outer literal content `  c` is preserved instead of the previous collapse to `a b` + ` c`. The helper still produces signatures like `public sealed class Foo<T> : BaseFoo<T>, IBar, IBaz where T : class, new()` for plain wrapped headers, and literal-bearing declarations like `record Foo(string S = "a  b")`, `@"C:\tmp\   spaces"`, `"""a   b"""`, multi-line raw-string primary-constructor defaults, and interpolation holes containing nested verbatim strings all keep every internal space and newline exactly as written. Same-line headers, single-line bodies, and the existing multi-line property path are unchanged. Added `SymbolExtractor` regression coverage for wrapped class + base list + `where` clauses, wrapped interface + multi-base + `where`, wrapped record primary constructor + wrapped base list + `where`, wrapped struct + `IEquatable<Value<T>>` + `where T : IComparable<T>`, wrapped enum + underlying type `: byte`, a same-line-class pin, dedicated wrapped-header + `//` line comment and wrapped-header + `/* ... */` block comment pins so comment-stripping cannot regress, wrapped primary-constructor-header pins for regular string, verbatim string, and raw string defaults so the lexer-aware collapse cannot silently rewrite literal whitespace, a multi-line raw-string default pin so newlines and per-line indentation inside multi-line raw strings cannot be destroyed by cross-line collapsing, and a nested-verbatim-inside-interpolation-hole pin so interpolation holes inside wrapped base-list arguments cannot exit the outer string too early and collapse inner literals. `BuildCSharpTypeHeaderSignature` also trims a trailing `'\r'` from every sliced line before appending the inter-line `'\n'`, so CRLF-terminated sources (Windows CI with `autocrlf=true`, files saved from Visual Studio, etc.) produce the same signature as LF-terminated sources instead of carrying OS-dependent `"\r\n"` separators between lines; a dedicated CRLF-content regression test pins that normalization. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/SymbolExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/SymbolExtractorTests.cs`. Closes #382.
- **Regression lock for out-of-range numeric query options (#161)** — `QueryCommandRunner` already rejects invalid `--limit` / `--depth` / `--before` / `--after` / `--start` / `--end` / `--snippet-lines` values with exit code 1, but the existing entrypoint coverage only exercised the non-parseable `"nope"` path. The original bug was specifically about valid integers (`0`, `-5`, `-1`) that parse successfully but fail the positive / non-negative constraint — those used to silently fall back to defaults and emit real results on stdout with exit 0, so callers that branch on exit code alone treated the default-backed output as authoritative. Added a dedicated regression theory `QueryEntrypoints_OutOfRangeNumericOptionsFailClosed_Issue161` that drives `RunSymbols`, `RunSearch`, `RunImpact`, and `RunExcerpt` with the exact repro values from the issue (`--limit 0` / `--limit -5`, `--snippet-lines 0`, `--depth -1`, `--start 0` / `--start -5`, `--end 0`, `--before -1`, `--after -1`) and pins three invariants at once: exit code is `UsageError`, stderr carries the expected `--<option> requires a ...` message with the offending raw value, and stdout is strictly empty so default-backed output cannot leak. Affected: `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/QueryCommandRunnerTests.cs`. Closes #161.
- **C# LINQ query-expression continuations no longer leak phantom method symbols (#377)** — The method regex and explicit-interface-implementation regex in `SymbolExtractor` now add the C# LINQ query-expression contextual keywords (`from`, `where`, `select`, `orderby`, `group`, `join`, `let`, `into`, `on`, `equals`, `ascending`, `descending`, `by`) to their statement-keyword negative lookaheads. Previously a continuation line like `where Validator.Check(x)` / `select Mapper.Convert(x)` / `orderby Math.Abs(x)` could satisfy the explicit-interface shape (`returnType=<linq-keyword>` + `qualifier.member(`) and emit phantom `function Check` / `function Convert` / `function Abs` rows alongside the real definitions, silently polluting `symbols`, `definition`, `callers`, `inspect`, and `hotspots` wherever qualified static helper calls appear inside LINQ query syntax. The lookahead is anchored to the line-leading token, so only bare continuation lines are rejected; regular method declarations whose name happens to be a LINQ keyword (such as `public void where() { }`) still match through their return type and are indexed as before. Added a `SymbolExtractor` regression test that locks the full LINQ query-expression repro (`where`, `select`, `orderby`, `group` / `by` / `into`, `join` / `on` / `equals`, `ascending`, `descending`, `let = ...`) with qualified static helper calls — every individual keyword appears in a line-leading position so each arm of the guard is exercised — and asserts that no phantom `function` rows surface for the helper member names and that real helper definitions still appear exactly once each. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/SymbolExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/SymbolExtractorTests.cs`, `DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`. Closes #377.
- **C# explicit-interface property implementations now surface as `property` symbols, and multi-argument generic qualifiers are honored on both explicit-interface properties and methods (#333)** — `SymbolExtractor` now matches both brace-body (`int IThing.Value { get; set; }`) and expression-body (`string IThing.Name => "x";`) explicit-interface property implementations with dedicated C# rows that mirror the existing explicit-interface method row: the interface qualifier is non-capturing so the short property name (`Value`, `Name`) is recorded as the symbol name, consistent with how `Dispose` and `CompareTo` are exposed for explicit-interface methods. The shared `CSharpExplicitInterfaceQualifierPattern` has also been widened to accept the same shape that `CSharpTypePattern` uses for regular return types — comma-separated type arguments with internal spaces, nullable-typed arguments, and array-typed arguments — so qualifiers like `IMap<string, int>.PairCount`, `IFoo<string?>.Nullable`, and `IFoo<int[]>.ArrayArg` no longer silently drop. Because both the property rows and the pre-existing method row share the qualifier pattern, the same fix also repairs explicit-interface methods with multi-argument generic qualifiers (for example `int IMap<string, int>.GetCount() => 0;`), which the previous narrower qualifier pattern had quietly skipped. Generic interface qualifiers like `IBucket<int>.Items`, generic / alias-qualified return types, and `ref readonly` explicit-interface properties are all supported. The statement-keyword negative lookahead mirrors the regular property rows so `return o switch { ... }` style expressions cannot misclassify as properties. Without the fix those declarations were silently dropped from `symbols`, `definition`, `references`, `callers`, `callees`, `inspect`, and `outline`. Added extractor regression coverage for brace-body, expression-body, generic-interface, `ref readonly`, multi-argument generic, nullable-argument, and array-argument explicit-interface property implementations, and extended the existing explicit-interface method regression with multi-argument generic, nullable-argument, and array-argument method forms. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/SymbolExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/SymbolExtractorTests.cs`, `DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`. Closes #333.
- **C# plain fields are now indexed as symbols (#298)** — `SymbolExtractor` previously only captured `const` and `static readonly` fields as C# symbols, so ordinary declarations like `public int Count;`, `private readonly List<int> _items;`, `protected volatile bool _ready;`, and `public static int GlobalCount;` were invisible to `definition`, `symbols`, `outline`, `inspect`, `hotspots`, and `unused`. Added a dedicated plain-field pattern that runs after the existing `const` / `static readonly` patterns and before the structural declaration patterns, captures the visibility and return type, and emits kind `property` (consistent with the taxonomy that already covers regular properties and record primary components). The terminator is `=(?![=>])` or `;`, which excludes methods (`(`), property accessors (`{`), expression-bodied members (`=>`), and comparison-operator overloads (`==`). The negative lookahead repeats every visibility and modifier keyword so the regex engine cannot backtrack past an unconsumed `public static event EventHandler OnClick;` declaration and misclassify it as a field whose returnType is `public static event EventHandler`. A scope tracker built from `StructuralLineMasker` output gates the new pattern to lines that sit directly inside a type body (`class` / `struct` / `interface` / `record` / `enum`), so local variable declarations inside method / property accessor / constructor / lambda bodies — which share the same shape as fields — are no longer misclassified as phantom `property` symbols and no longer leak into `symbols`, `definition`, `outline`, `inspect`, or `unused`. Field detection also extends beyond the single-line shape: the match line is now concatenated across multiple physical lines until the terminating `;` is reached (so `private Dictionary<string, int>` on one line followed by `    _map = new();` on the next is indexed as a single `_map` field with return type `Dictionary<string,int>`), the multi-line header prefix also accepts field-only modifiers such as `volatile`, `unsafe`, and `extern` so declarations like `private volatile Dictionary<string, int>\n    _map;` are no longer rejected at the header-prefix gate, the continuation walk tracks paren/bracket/brace depth until a top-level `;` is reached so parenthesized initializers such as `private Lazy<int>\n    _value = new(\n        () => 42);` merge all the way through the `(` instead of short-circuiting at the first parenthesis, multi-line fields whose initializer opens its own object or collection initializer — such as `private Dictionary<string, int>\n    _map = new()\n    {\n        ["a"] = 1\n    };`, `private List<int>\n    _list = new() {\n        1, 2, 3\n    };`, and `private Dictionary<string, int>\n    _typed = new Dictionary<string, int>\n    {\n        ["b"] = 2\n    };` — now continue past the initializer braces until the real top-level `;` closes the declaration (the accessor check still claims genuine property bodies first, so `{` is only treated as initializer scope once it is known not to start a property block), brace detection against the combined match line now runs on the structurally sanitized line instead of the raw source so `{` appearing inside a string literal or comment (for example `private string\n    _open = "{";` and `private string\n    _pair = "{" + "}";`) no longer flips the multi-line field path into property-body handling and silently drops the declaration, declarator lists such as `private int _x, _y;`, `public string First, Second, Third;`, and `private int _a = 1, _b, _c = 3;` now emit one symbol per declarator (each with the shared return type and its own per-declarator initializer stripped) instead of one symbol whose `return_type` silently contains a trailing comma, the declarator-list tail scanner now distinguishes generic `<`/`>` from comparison operators via a token-aware lookahead so initializers like `private int _a = x < y ? 1 : 2, _b;` or `private int _e = new Dictionary<int, int>() { [x < y ? 1 : 2] = 0 }.Count, _f;` no longer inflate the angle depth indefinitely and drop the trailing declarators, and the `delegate\b` negative lookahead is relaxed to `delegate\b(?!\*)` so function-pointer fields like `public delegate*<int, void> Callback;` and `private delegate* unmanaged[Cdecl]<int, int> _op;` pass through the plain-field path while real `public delegate int Callback(int x);` type declarations still continue to be handled by the dedicated `delegate` pattern. Added regression coverage for instance, readonly, volatile, plain static, protected-with-initializer, internal-volatile, and generic `Dictionary<string, int>` field shapes, for multi-line field declarations that wrap before `;`, for multi-line fields that rely on `volatile` / `unsafe` modifiers and function-pointer return types, for multi-line fields whose initializer uses a constructor call or parenthesized expression (including bodies that contain a lambda), for multi-line fields whose initializer uses object / collection initializers with `new() { ... };`, `new() { ... };` on a same-line brace, and `new Dictionary<...> { ... };`, for multi-line fields whose initializer contains `{` inside a string literal, for declarator-list fields (including mixed-initializer shapes and an assertion that no emitted symbol ever has a comma-contaminated `return_type`), for declarator-list fields whose initializer uses comparison operators inside generic-shaped constructs, for `delegate*` and `delegate* unmanaged[Cdecl]` function-pointer fields, plus a negative test pinning that real named-`delegate` type declarations are not misclassified as fields, a dedicated negative test that locks ctor-locals, method-locals, nested-block-locals, accessor-locals, and lambda-body-locals out of the symbol index, and a CLI end-to-end `QueryCommandRunner.RunSymbols` test that round-trips the multi-line / declarator-list / function-pointer shapes through indexer, DB, and `symbols --exact`, updated the developer guide C# language-pattern row to call out the new field coverage, and updated the README query-strategy section (English and Japanese) so users and AI clients see `public int Count;`, `private readonly List<int> _items;`, `public delegate*<int, void> Callback;`, and `cdidx symbols --lang csharp --kind property --name Count --exact-name` as first-class examples. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/SymbolExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/SymbolExtractorTests.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/QueryCommandRunnerTests.cs`, `DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`, `README.md`. Closes #298.
- **C# inline and standalone attributes with bracket-bearing string literals no longer mis-bucket adjacent symbols in `unused` (#375)** — `DbSymbolReader.StripLeadingCSharpAttributeLists` was called on raw source lines without sanitizing C# string literals, so an inline attribute whose argument string contained `[` or `]` (e.g. `[JsonPropertyName("a[")] public string X { get; set; }`) was mis-parsed as "no inline declaration" by `LineContainsInlineAttributeAndDeclaration`. `GetAdjacentAttributeBlock` then treated that line as a free-standing attribute block and leaked the attribute context to the next property line, causing an adjacent plain property to be incorrectly classified as `reflection_or_config_suspect` in `unused`. The same class of bug also surfaced on the standalone-attribute path: `GetAdjacentAttributeBlock`'s upward scan used `CountChar(line, ']') - CountChar(line, '[')` to track bracket depth, so a standalone attribute line like `[Obsolete("]")]` above an unrelated property left one phantom bracket of depth and swallowed the previous member's reflection attribute block upward. The indexer path in `SymbolExtractor` was not affected because it already feeds `LexCSharpLine`-sanitized input into its strip. The DB-reader strip is now string-literal aware via a new `TrySkipCSharpStringOrCharLiteral` helper covering regular `"..."`, verbatim `@"..."`, raw `"""..."""` (C# 11, including longer quote runs), interpolated `$"..."`, interpolated verbatim `$@"..."` / `@$"..."`, raw interpolated `$"""..."""` and multi-`$` variants like `$$"""..."""` (where N consecutive `$` require N consecutive `{` / `}` to open / close interpolation while fewer are literal), and char `'...'` literals, `GetAdjacentAttributeBlock`'s standalone upward scan now uses a new `CountBracketDeltaOutsideStrings` helper that reuses the same string-literal skipper instead of naive `CountChar`, and the function refuses to carry an attribute block across a line that already declares a member on the same line. Added regression coverage that pins both the inline "adjacent plain property is not suspect" and "inline reflection attribute with bracket-in-string is still suspect" shapes, including verbatim, raw, raw-interpolated, and multi-`$` raw-interpolated variants, plus a standalone-attribute regression where a `[Obsolete("]")]` on its own line above a plain property must not swallow a real reflection attribute above it. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Database/DbSymbolReader.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/DbReaderTests.cs`. Closes #375.
- **T-SQL `EXEC` / `EXECUTE` / `CALL` stored-procedure references without trailing parens are now captured (#232)** — `ReferenceExtractor` previously only matched SQL procedure calls through the shared `CallRegex`, which requires a trailing `(` after the identifier. Real-world T-SQL almost exclusively uses the no-parens form (`EXEC dbo.sp_Target @a=1, @b=2;`, `EXECUTE [dbo].[sp_Target];`, MySQL / MariaDB `CALL sp_Target;`, `EXEC @retval = dbo.sp_Target ...`), so stored-procedure calls silently disappeared from `references`, `inspect`, `callers`, and `impact` on SQL codebases, leaving cross-procedure chains invisible. A new compiled regex `SqlProcCallRegex` locates `EXEC` / `EXECUTE` / `CALL` at word boundaries, optionally skips T-SQL return-value assignment (`@retval =`), and captures the terminal identifier (including `[bracketed names]` and multi-part `[dbo].[proc]` forms), stripping any enclosing brackets and adjusting the emitted column so the reference points at the identifier's real position. The match is case-insensitive and runs against the sanitized line produced by `PrepareLine`, so `EXEC` inside a string literal or comment is still naturally ignored. Ambiguous keywords that follow `EXECUTE` in other dialects — `AS` (T-SQL `EXECUTE AS USER='...'`) and `IMMEDIATE` (Oracle `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE ...`) — are added to the SQL ignore list with case-insensitive comparison so they can no longer surface as phantom procedure calls. The SQL ignore list also rejects the keywords `EXEC` / `EXECUTE` / `CALL` themselves so that T-SQL dynamic-SQL forms such as `EXEC(@sql)`, `EXEC('SELECT 1')`, and `EXECUTE(@sql)` — where the argument is a string or variable, not an identifier — cannot trigger a phantom `call EXEC` / `call EXECUTE` / `call CALL` edge through the generic `CallRegex`. Bracketed T-SQL identifiers (used in real code specifically to quote reserved words as object names, e.g. `EXEC [ORDER]`, `CALL [USER]`, `EXEC [dbo].[IMMEDIATE]`) skip the keyword ignore list after bracket stripping, so legitimate brace-quoted proc names whose inner text happens to match a SQL keyword are no longer silently dropped. A dedup key of `{lineNumber}:{column}:{referenceKind}:{name}` ensures the parenthesized form (`EXEC dbo.sp_Target();` and its bracketed variant `EXEC [dbo].[sp_Target]()`) still emits a single edge when both `SqlProcCallRegex` and the generic `CallRegex` would fire at the same position — `SqlProcCallRegex`'s post-bracket-stripping column adjustment keeps the two regexes converging on the same dedup key. Added regression tests in `ReferenceExtractorTests.cs` covering: no-parens extraction across `EXEC` / `EXECUTE` / `CALL` with plain, qualified, bracketed, and multi-segment bracketed forms; linked-server four-part names `EXEC server.db.schema.proc`; return-value assignment form; `EXECUTE AS USER='dbo'` / `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'sql'` negative coverage; string-literal safety (`EXEC sp_InsideString` inside a literal does not emit, but the outer `EXEC sp_executesql @sql` does); dedup parity between the parenthesized and no-parens forms (both plain and bracketed); the MySQL `CALL proc(args)` form with arguments; Unicode bracketed identifiers (`[名前]`, `[Ñoño]`, `[Процедура]`); `EXEC(@sql)` / `EXEC('...')` / `EXECUTE(@sql)` / `CALL(@sql)` dynamic-SQL negative coverage that pins no phantom EXEC / EXECUTE / CALL keyword edges; bracketed reserved-word identifier coverage (`[ORDER]`, `[AS]`, `[IMMEDIATE]`, `[USER]`) that pins legitimate calls survive after bracket stripping; and a non-word bracketed identifier coverage (`[#tempProc]` for T-SQL temp procedures, `[proc-name]` for hyphenated names, `[proc.v2]` for dotted versioned names) that pins the bracket character class accepts any character except `[`, `]`, or a line terminator so temp-proc and hyphenated real-world identifiers are captured and the preceding qualifier `[dbo]` is not misattributed as the proc name; omitted-qualifier-segment coverage (`EXEC AdventureWorks..sp_GetCustomer;`, `EXEC [AdventureWorks]..[proc-name];`, `EXEC srv.db..sp_with_omitted_schema;`) that pins SQL Server's four-part naming with a skipped database or schema still terminates on the real procedure name rather than falling back to the first qualifier segment; MySQL / MariaDB backtick-quoted identifier coverage (`` CALL `proc-name`; ``, `` CALL db.`proc-name`; ``, `` CALL `mydb`.`do_stuff`; ``) that pins backtick quoting is preserved through line sanitization and the terminal identifier is the captured target without the qualifier surfacing as a phantom call; and a backtick-quoted reserved-word coverage (`` CALL `order`; ``, `` CALL `select`; ``) that pins the ignore-list bypass after quote stripping, mirroring the existing bracketed `[ORDER]` / `[AS]` behavior. The internal identifier character class in `SqlProcCallRegex` therefore accepts three forms — `\[[^\[\]\r\n]+\]`, `` `[^`\r\n]+` ``, or bare `\w+` — in both qualifier and terminal-name positions, and qualifier segments themselves are optional so consecutive dots (`..`) do not abort the match. A dedicated `SqlStringLiteralRegex` + `PrepareSqlLineForIdentifierScan` helper sanitizes SQL lines for the `EXEC` / `EXECUTE` / `CALL` scan: unlike the shared `PrepareLine` it keeps backtick content intact (because backticks are identifier quoting in SQL, not string literals) while still stripping `'...'` / `"..."` literals and `--` / `#` / `/* ... */` comments so text inside a comment does not emit a phantom reference. The `--` and `#` line-comment scans track backtick and bracket identifier quoting so a legitimate `` CALL `proc#1`; `` or `EXEC [proc-name]` is not truncated mid-identifier even when the inner text contains `#` or `-`. A regression test `Extract_SqlHashCommentedCall_DoesNotEmitReference` pins the MySQL `# ...` comment behavior and a `Extract_SqlCallBacktickIdentifierContainingHash_IsCaptured` pin keeps `` CALL `proc#1`; `` alive. Also mentions `MySQL / MariaDB` rather than `SQL-PSM` in documentation, since the current implementation intentionally does not treat ANSI / SQL-PSM `"..."` delimited identifiers as identifier quoting (they still run through the string stripper). Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/ReferenceExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/ReferenceExtractorTests.cs`, `README.md`. Closes #232.
- **C# / Java constructor chain calls `: this(...)` / `: base(...)` / `super(...)` now show up as references (#257)** — `ReferenceExtractor` now rewrites C# constructor initializer chains and the equivalent Java constructor-body statements into `call` references pointing at the real target: `: this(args)` / `this(args);` resolves to the enclosing class or record, while `: base(args)` / `super(args);` parses the base type from the enclosing class signature (stripping generics, record primary-ctor args, `where` constraints, `global::` / dotted namespace qualifiers, and ignoring trailing interface entries in the base list). Cross-line C# initializers are attributed to the owning constructor rather than the enclosing class, C# records with `Parent(Value)` primary-ctor chaining get a synthetic function-kind container named after the record so the base call is attributed to the record itself instead of no container at all — the synthetic container now spans the full record declaration header up to the first `;` or `{`, so continuation-line forms like `public record Child(int Value, int Extra)\n    : Parent(Value);` attribute the base call to the record instead of leaving it in no container. Base-type parsing on both languages now uses a depth-aware scanner that splits on `.` / `::` at generic depth 0 and returns the terminal segment, so nested types under generic outer types such as `Outer<int>.Base` (C#), `Outer<Integer>.Base` (Java), and `global::Ns.Outer<T>.Inner` now resolve to `Base` / `Inner` instead of being misattributed to `Outer` and silently mis-aimed in `callers` / `callees` / `impact`. C# `: base(...)` resolution now reconstructs the full enclosing type header from structural lines (reusing the record primary-ctor header helper) instead of trusting `SymbolRecord.Signature`, which only captures the first declaration line, so formatter-style multi-line base-lists such as `class Child\n    : Parent`, `class Child<T>\n    : Outer<T>.Base`, and `class Child<T>\n    : Parent<T>\n    where T : class, new()` no longer silently drop the chain edge. Java `super(...)` resolution mirrors the same reconstruction, so multi-line `extends` forms such as `class Leaf\n    extends Base { Leaf(){super(0);} }`, `class Leaf\n    extends Outer<Integer>.Base {...}`, and `sealed class Leaf\n    extends Base\n    permits None` no longer drop the chain edge either. Java 17+ sealed-type declarations are supported too: the Java base-type scanner now treats `permits` as a word-boundary terminator alongside `implements`, so `sealed class Leaf extends Base permits A, B { Leaf(){super(0);} }` and `extends Outer<Integer>.Base permits A` resolve to `Base` instead of greedily absorbing `permits` into the returned type. Java package-private constructors that SymbolExtractor records without body ranges are found by a name-based fallback against the enclosing class so `Leaf(int x){super(x);}` still attributes the chain edge to the `Leaf` constructor, Java same-line ctor bodies such as `Leaf(int x){super(x);}` / `Leaf(){this(0);}` (which SymbolExtractor skips because the line ends with `}` instead of `{`/`,`/`;`) are handled by relaxing the ctor-chain regex to also match after `{` and by synthesizing a ctor container directly from the declaration line. The declaration-line scanner is depth-aware so it accepts fully qualified annotations with optional nested-paren argument lists (e.g. `@demo.Ann Leaf(int x){super(x);}`, `@SuppressWarnings({"unused", "unchecked"}) Leaf(...)`) and nested generic bounds on ctor type parameters (e.g. `public <T extends Comparable<Integer>> Leaf(T x){super(0);}`, `<U extends java.util.List<? extends Number>> Leaf(...)`), so annotated and generic same-line ctors are no longer silently dropped as class-scope phantom edges, and Java `this(...)` is added to the Java ignore set so the generic call scanner does not emit a phantom `call this` edge after the chain is rewritten. Java `super.method()` is still left alone as a regular call. `callers`, `references`, `callees`, and `impact` now surface the missing chain edges so a rename of a base constructor no longer looks safe when every subclass constructor chains to it. Java base-type resolution also strips JLS 9.7.4 type-use annotations before extracting the terminal segment, so `class Leaf extends @Ann Root`, `extends @pkg.Ann(value=1) Root`, `extends @Ann @Other Root`, and `extends Outer<Integer>.@Ann Base` resolve to the real base type instead of a phantom `@Ann Root` / `@Ann Base` name that silently misattributes `super(...)` edges. The base-list scanner also tracks `(...)` depth alongside `<...>` depth so commas inside annotation arguments such as `@Ann(a = 1, b = 2) Root`, `@Ann({A.class, B.class}) Root`, and `@pkg.Ann(value = {1, 2, 3}) Root` are no longer mistaken for top-level base-list separators (which previously truncated the segment before the annotation stripper could run and dropped the `super(...)` edge entirely). Java enums can declare constructors and chain via `this(...)`, so the enclosing-type candidate list and the innermost-class-like lookup now include `enum` alongside `class` / `struct` / `interface`; `enum Shade { Red, Blue(1); Shade(){ this(0); } Shade(int code){} }` now emits the chain edge to the enum instead of being silently dropped (C# enum is a no-op here because it cannot declare constructors and the C# chain regex never matches inside one). Added regression coverage for C# `: this(...)` / `: base(...)` (including generic bases, records attributed to the synthetic constructor, multi-line record continuation-line base calls, braced record bodies after a base call, cross-line wraps, `global::` base types, nested types under generic outer types such as `Outer<int>.Base` and `global::Ns.Outer<T>.Inner`, plain multi-line class base-lists like `class Child\n    : Parent`, multi-line nested-generic base-lists like `class Child<T>\n    : Outer<T>.Base`, and multi-line base-lists followed by `where` constraints) and Java `super(...)` / `this(...)` (including package-private constructors, public and package-private same-line ctor bodies for both `super(...)` and `this(...)`, same-line ctor bodies with leading annotations, same-line ctor bodies with generic type parameters, fully qualified annotations with nested-paren argument lists, nested generic bounds on ctor type parameters, nested types under generic outer types such as `Outer<Integer>.Base`, sealed / non-sealed / `permits`-bearing declarations including `extends Outer<Integer>.Base permits A`, multi-line `extends` base-lists like `class Leaf\n    extends Base`, multi-line `extends Outer<Integer>.Base`, multi-line `extends` with continuation-line `permits`, JLS 9.7.4 type-use annotated `extends` (`extends @Ann Root`, `extends @pkg.Ann Root`, `extends @Ann(value=1) Root`, `extends @Ann @Other Root`, `extends Outer<Integer>.@Ann Base`, `extends @Ann Outer<Integer>.Base`, `extends @Ann Root implements Foo`) including the E2E `super(...)` paths that would have pointed at a phantom annotated type, Java enum `this(...)` constructor chain attribution, and phantom `this` suppression). Java same-line ctor name extraction now accepts `@annotation` and `public` / `protected` / `private` / `static` / `final` / `abstract` modifiers in any order so formatter-style forms like `public @Deprecated Leaf(int x){super(x);}` and `@demo.Ann private Leaf(){this(0);}` no longer silently drop the chain edge when an annotation sits between modifiers instead of before them. The multi-line header collector is also depth-aware in `()` / `[]` / `<>` depth so `{` / `;` inside annotation arguments, array initializers, or generic bounds (e.g. `extends @Ann({A.class, B.class}) Root {`) no longer truncate the enclosing-type header before the real base type; this helper feeds both Java multi-line `extends` resolution and C# record primary-ctor container synthesis. `SymbolExtractor.FindBraceRange` is now also depth-aware in `()` / `[]` so that `{` / `}` inside annotation-argument and attribute-argument braces (`@Ann({A.class, B.class})`, array-initializer arguments, annotation-nested `{}`) do not count as body braces and no longer collapse the enclosing type's body range to a single line. Without that fix, `class Leaf extends @Ann({A.class, B.class}) Root { Leaf() { super(0); } }` would index `Leaf` with a one-line body range, so the `super(0)` call-site fell outside the Leaf class and no ctor body was recognized, silently dropping the `super(...)` chain edge from `callers` / `references` / `impact` even with the depth-aware ReferenceExtractor header collector in place. The same `FindBraceRange` depth tracking now also honors block comments (`/* ... */`), line comments (`//`), string literals (`"..."`), and Rust / OCaml-style lifetime annotations (`'a`, `'static`) separately from real single-character literals (`'x'`, `'\n'`), so unbalanced `(`, `[`, `{`, or `}` tokens living inside comments or strings can no longer break the body range. In parallel, `ReferenceExtractor.CollectCSharpRecordHeader` no longer tracks `<` / `>` as generic depth — which previously reacted to comparison operators such as `[Attr(Flag = 1 < 2)]` and extended the synthetic C# primary-ctor container all the way to EOF, incorrectly attributing body calls after the real `{` to the record ctor — and now masks comment / string / char-literal content to spaces before appending it to the joined header buffer, so `class Leaf extends Root /* ( stray [ */ { ... super(0); ... }`-style headers round-trip cleanly through `ParseCSharpBaseType` / `ParseJavaBaseType` without the masked noise poisoning base-type resolution. Added an E2E regression test that rebuilds both SymbolExtractor symbols and ReferenceExtractor edges for a brace-annotation `extends` fixture and asserts the `Root` call lands inside the Leaf ctor body, plus a `CollectCSharpRecordHeader` comparison-operator regression test and an E2E C# primary-ctor regression test that locks the attribute-argument comparison operator and comment / string noise cases against header-scoped container synthesis. The shared Java balanced-paren scanners `SkipBalancedParens` and `StripJavaTypeAnnotations` are now string / char-literal aware, so annotations with quoted arguments such as `extends @Ann(text=")") Root` (base-type resolution) and `public @Ann(text=")") Leaf(){super(0);}` (same-line ctor name extraction) no longer close early on a `)` embedded inside a string literal, which previously mangled base-type segments to `") Root` and silently dropped the `super(...)` chain edge on otherwise legal Java. Added E2E regression coverage for both the annotated `extends` and same-line ctor paths, plus a direct `TryExtractJavaCtorNameFromLine` unit test locking the quoted-argument annotation scan. `SymbolExtractor.FindBraceRange` now also takes a language hint and treats `'...'` as a full string literal in PHP (scanning to the next unescaped `'` regardless of distance), rather than falling back to the Rust/OCaml lifetime-vs-char-literal heuristic. Without this split, long PHP default arguments like `function demo($x = 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa[') { return callThing(); }` leaked the `[` into `bracketDepth`, pinned the body-brace state above zero, collapsed `demo`'s body range to null, and dropped `callThing`'s container so `callers` / `references` / `impact` lost the attribution. Added a PHP regression test that locks the function body range and the `callThing -> function:demo` edge. The C# primary-ctor synthetic container range now also tracks a start column at the `class` / `struct` / `record` keyword on the declaration line, so attribute-argument calls that textually precede the keyword (for example `[Attr(Helper.Get())] public class Child(int x) : Parent(x) {}`) stay attributed to the real `class:Child` container instead of being misattributed to the synthetic `function:Child` ctor. Without that scoping, `callers Attr` / `callers Helper.Get` / `impact` all showed phantom child-ctor callers for every attribute evaluated before the class declaration. Added a regression test that locks `Attr` and `Helper.Get` on the class container while `Parent(x)` stays on the synthetic function ctor. Added regression coverage for Java same-line modifier-before-annotation ctors and for the depth-aware header collector directly. C# record primary-ctor container synthesis no longer relies on a first-line regex over `SymbolRecord.Signature` for gating: the stored signature only captures the first declaration line, so split-line forms like `public record Child\n(\n    int Value\n)\n    : Parent(Value);` were silently excluded and the `Parent(Value)` edge collapsed onto class/no-container instead of the synthetic record ctor. The gate now runs on the joined multi-line header produced by `CollectCSharpRecordHeader`, so split-line record primary-ctors with multi-line `: base(...)` continuations also attribute the chain edge to the synthetic function-kind container named after the record; added a direct regression test covering that split-line shape. The synthetic record-ctor container is also applied at call-site granularity rather than line-level: `CollectCSharpRecordHeader` now reports the terminator column on the end line, and the override only replaces the container for call-site matches whose column sits inside the header span. Without this scoping, legal same-line bodies like `record Child(int V) : Parent(V) { public int Sum() => Add(V, 1); }` silently handed `Add(...)` to the synthetic record ctor even though it lives past the header-terminating `{` and belongs to a real body-level container, polluting `callers` / `impact` with phantom record-ctor callers. The record-header detector now also tracks generic / bracket depth when looking for the primary-ctor `(` in the first base-list entry so that tuple-type interface implementations such as `record Pair(int A, int B) : IBox<(int Left, int Right)>` (where `(` appears inside `<...>`) are no longer mistaken for a primary-ctor base call, which previously synthesized a phantom record-ctor container over the whole declaration line and misattributed unrelated body calls. Synthetic primary-ctor container generation has also been generalized from C# records to C# 12 `class` and `struct` primary constructors: `public class Child(int value) : Parent(value)`, the split-line form `public class ChildSplit\n(\n    int value\n) : Parent(\n    value\n)`, generic forms like `public class GenericChild<T>(T value) : Parent(42)`, same-line braced bodies like `public class ChildWithBody(int value) : Parent(value) { public int Doubled { get; } = Helper.Compute(value); }`, and struct primary ctors like `public struct BoxedValue(int value) : BaseImpl(value)` now all attribute the base-list primary-ctor call to a synthetic `function`-kind container named after the enclosing type instead of collapsing onto the class itself or no container at all. The header-end column scoping still applies so body calls past the header-terminating `{` stay attributed to their real inner container. Added regression coverage for the same-line braced-body and tuple-in-base-list record shapes as well as class (same-line, split-line, generic, same-line braced body) and struct C# 12 primary-ctor shapes. Java same-line ctor non-chain body calls now also attribute to a synthetic `function:<CtorName>` container instead of leaking to the enclosing `class:<CtorName>`: the main loop pre-computes a per-line Java ctor span via a shared depth-aware walker (the same walker that already resolved the ctor name for chain rewrites) and flows it through the container override used by the generic `CallRegex` path, so `public <T> Leaf(T x){super(0); Helper.doWork();}` finally surfaces `Helper.doWork` as a caller of `function:Leaf` rather than pretending the class itself invoked it, and the surrounding `callers` / `references` / `impact` views reflect what the ctor actually does. The same span also suppresses the bogus `CtorName|call|class|CtorName` edge that `CallRegex` previously emitted for the declarator `CtorName(` on a same-line ctor shape (since the declarator is a declaration site, not a call). Added regression coverage for both the body-call attribution (`Helper.doWork` landing on `function:Leaf` in a generic-annotated same-line ctor) and the declarator self-call suppression (`Leaf(){super(0);}` no longer emitting `Leaf|call|class|Leaf`). Java base-type resolution now also locates the class-level `extends` via a depth-aware scan that ignores `extends` keywords appearing inside `<...>` (bounded type parameters) and `(...)` (annotation argument lists), so bounded generic subclasses like `class Leaf<T extends Number> extends Root`, `class Leaf<A extends Number, B extends CharSequence> extends Root`, `class Leaf<T extends Number & Comparable<T>> extends Root`, and `class Leaf<T extends List<? extends Number>> extends Root` finally resolve to the real base type rather than grabbing the first textual `extends` (which pointed at the bound `Number`) — the previous first-match behavior caused `super(...)` to silently resolve against the type-parameter bound on otherwise legal Java, skewing `callers` / `references` / `impact` for every bounded-generic subclass. Added a direct `ParseJavaBaseType` bounded-generic unit test and an end-to-end `Extract_JavaSuperCall_BoundedTypeParameter_AttributesToRealBase` regression that locks the `super(0)` edge to `Root` for `class Leaf<T extends Number> extends Root { Leaf(){ super(0); } }`. The Java structural ctor fallback (used when SymbolExtractor does not emit a function symbol for the plain-form ctor) now walks enclosing-type bodies with the same depth-aware header detector used by the same-line path and delegates body-range resolution to `SymbolExtractor.FindJavaBraceRange` instead of requiring `)` and `{` to share the declaration line, so Allman-style ctor bodies (`Leaf()\n{\n    super(0);\n}`), ctors whose parameter lists span multiple lines (`Leaf(\n    int a,\n    int b\n) { super(a, b); }`), and ctors with multi-line `throws` clauses (`Leaf(int x)\n    throws IoFailure\n{\n    super(x);\n}`) no longer silently drop the chain edge. `SymbolExtractor.FindJavaBraceRange` gained `()` / `[]` / `<>` depth tracking before the body opens, so `{` / `}` inside type-use annotation arguments or bounded generics (`class Leaf extends @Ann({A.class, B.class}) Root {`) cannot prematurely open or close the enclosing class body, keeping the downstream `super(...)` resolution intact. Added `Extract_JavaSuperCall_AllmanCtorBody_AttributesToRealBase`, `Extract_JavaSuperCall_MultiLineParameterList_AttributesToRealBase`, and `Extract_JavaSuperCall_MultiLineThrowsClause_AttributesToRealBase` regression tests to lock the multi-line ctor attribution end to end. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/ReferenceExtractor.cs`, `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/SymbolExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/ReferenceExtractorTests.cs`. Closes #257.

### [1.11.0] - 2026-04-17

#### Changed
- **Windows CI test run no longer pays Windows Defender overhead on `windows-latest` (#394)** — The `Build and Test` workflow previously saw Windows test duration range roughly 5–13 minutes versus ~36s on Ubuntu and ~51s on macOS for the same sequential xUnit suite, with the top of that range attributed to Windows Defender real-time scanning of every temp project, SQLite DB, `.cdidx/` directory, and synthetic source file created by the tests on the `windows-latest` runner. Added a Windows-only `Exclude workspace and temp paths from Windows Defender` step before `Set up .NET` in both `.github/workflows/dotnet.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml` that calls `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath` for the workspace plus every candidate temp root: `$RUNNER_TEMP`, `$TEMP`, `$TMP`, and the live `[System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()` value (trailing separators stripped before dedup). `$TMP` and the runtime `GetTempPath()` call are included because .NET's `Path.GetTempPath()` consults `TMP` before `TEMP` and may resolve to a path that differs from `$env:TEMP` in pwsh. `-ExclusionProcess` is intentionally not used because it requires full image paths — bare filenames like `dotnet.exe` would silently fail to register, and the test suite's temp files all live under the excluded paths anyway. The final effective exclusion list is echoed to the log for debuggability. Every `Add-MpPreference` call uses `-ErrorAction Stop`, and a final `Get-MpPreference` verification throws if any exclusion did not register, so the step fails loudly instead of silently degrading. This is a CI-only change scoped to the ephemeral Windows runner, does not touch production or test code, and does not relax xUnit's assembly-level `DisableTestParallelization` serialization contract. Affected: `.github/workflows/dotnet.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Closes #394.
- **Developer Guide now distinguishes SQLite's role from "zero dependencies" and labels release numbers as examples** — Clarified that cdidx remains a zero-configuration, single-file CLI with exactly one production dependency (`Microsoft.Data.Sqlite`), and made the release-workflow checklist explicitly state that `1.9.0` is only an example version to substitute during an actual release. Affected: `DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md`.

#### Fixed
- **`deps` C# attribute suffix alias now only matches class-like targets, and `impact` metadata bypass is suppressed when the class-like target name is ambiguous across namespaces (#293 follow-up)** — The earlier `#293` follow-up made `deps` UNION a C#-only `symbol_name || 'Attribute'` suffix alias into the logical-reference CTE so `[Foo]` attribute consumers could reach `FooAttribute` class files, and made `impact` (`GetFileDependencyHintsToResolvedType`) bypass the structured-evidence guard whenever any contributing reference was `attribute` / `annotation`. Both changes were too broad. On `deps` the alias joined purely by name, so `[Foo]` would also depend on any file that merely defined a function / property / variable named `FooAttribute` (e.g. `void MyAuditAttribute()` in an unrelated helper). On `impact` the metadata bypass did not check whether the target name was uniquely a class-like definition, so when the same unqualified name (e.g. `MyAuditAttribute`) existed in multiple namespaces the rename/remove blast radius was over-reported — attribute / annotation reference rows only keep the short name and cannot be disambiguated. `DbReader.GetFileDependencies` now tags synthetic alias rows with `is_attribute_alias = 1` (real rows are `0`), propagates the flag through `source_name_counts` via `MIN`, and restricts alias edges to class-like target kinds (`class` / `struct` / `interface`) in the `edges` CTE join. The `target_files` CTE is also switched from `DISTINCT` over `(path, lang, name, kind)` to `GROUP BY (path, lang, name)` with a `MAX(...)` `has_class_like_kind` flag, so files that define both a class and a same-named function (e.g. the C# constructor `Target()` inside `class Target`) no longer fan out into two target rows and inflate the `deps` reference count. `DbReader.GetFileDependencyHintsToResolvedType` now calls a new `IsMetadataTargetUnambiguous(definition, lang, pathPatterns, excludePathPatterns, excludeTests)` helper that counts class-like definitions with the same unqualified name *within the active impact scope* (graph-supported languages, plus the caller's `--lang` / `--path` / `--exclude-path` / `--exclude-tests` filters); the metadata evidence-guard bypass is only applied when that in-scope count is ≤ 1. If the name is ambiguous within scope, metadata-only edges fall through to the normal `SourceFileHasStructuredTypeEvidence` check, so pure `[MyAudit]` consumers are dropped instead of being mis-attributed. Scoping matters: a same-named class in an unrelated language / path / test tree must not suppress the C# metadata bypass, because attribute reference rows are already language-qualified through the graph-supported reference join, and the README contract for `impact` explicitly promises "active `--lang` / `--path` / `--exclude-path` / `--exclude-tests` scope". The C# attribute deps test `GetFileDependencies_MatchesCSharpAttributeSuffixConvention`, the unambiguous single-definition `impact` test, and the pre-existing graph-queries dedupe test all still pass. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpAttributeAliasOnlyMatchesClassLikeTargets` (ambiguous same-name function must not produce a spurious edge), `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_SuppressesCSharpAttributeMetadataBypassOnAmbiguousTarget` (two `MyAuditAttribute` classes within the same impact scope suppress the metadata heuristic hint), `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_CSharpAttributeMetadataBypassAppliesWhenTargetUnambiguous` (single class definition still surfaces the `[MyAudit]` consumer), `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_MetadataBypassAmbiguityGuard_RespectsLangScope` (same-named Java annotation must not suppress a `--lang csharp` query), `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_MetadataBypassAmbiguityGuard_RespectsPathScope` (out-of-scope `src/B/` same-named class must not suppress a `src/A/`-scoped query), and `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_MetadataBypassAmbiguityGuard_RespectsExcludeTests` (test-tree same-named class must not suppress an `--exclude-tests` query). `ResolveImpactFallbackNames` is additionally tightened so the C# `Attribute`-suffix alias is only applied to the resolved definition's own name: previously the alias was applied to every same-file fallback name, so a nested `BarAttribute` inside the file that defines `FooAttribute` caused `impact FooAttribute` to falsely attribute `[Bar]` use sites to `FooAttribute`'s blast radius. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_CSharpAttributeSuffixAlias_DoesNotLeakToSameFileSiblings` to pin this. `GetFileDependencies` is additionally restructured so metadata rows (`attribute` / `annotation`) cannot leak onto bare-name call-graph targets: the `logical_references` CTE now carries an `is_metadata` flag, `source_name_counts` groups by `(source_file_id, source_path, source_lang, symbol_name, is_attribute_alias, is_metadata)` so metadata and non-metadata rows with the same symbol_name stay separate, the `edges` CTE restricts ALL metadata edges (not just synthetic aliases) to `tf.has_class_like_kind = 1`, and two new CTEs resolve the remaining false-positive shapes: `metadata_raw_suppression` drops the raw C# `[Foo]` row when the synthetic `FooAttribute` alias already resolves to a class-like target in the same source file (so `[Foo]` does not fan out to both `class FooAttribute` and a plain `class Foo` that shares the bare name), and `target_ambiguity` drops metadata edges when the same-named symbol resolves to multiple class-like definitions in scope (so ambiguous `[MyAudit]` usage is left to `impact` / `references` to disambiguate rather than being fanned out to every same-named attribute class). The existing `GetFileDependencies_IncludesMetadataReferencesAsCompileTimeDependencies` test (which pins `[JsonConverter(...)]` → `class JsonConverter : Attribute` for a target class whose name does NOT end in `Attribute`) still passes because only one class-like target exists in scope, so `target_ambiguity` keeps it, the `is_metadata` / class-like restriction accepts it, and `metadata_raw_suppression` finds no synthetic `JsonConverterAttribute` alias target and therefore does not suppress the raw row. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpAttributeRawDoesNotLeakToBareNameClass_WhenSuffixTargetExists` (raw `[MyAudit]` row is suppressed when the alias resolves to `class MyAuditAttribute`, so `[MyAudit]` does NOT depend on an unrelated plain `class MyAudit` file), `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpAttributeDoesNotLeakToSameNameMethodOrProperty` (fully-qualified `[MyAuditAttribute]` metadata does NOT depend on a file that only defines a method / property named `MyAuditAttribute`), and `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpAttributeDoesNotFanOutWhenMultipleSameNameAttributeClasses` (two same-named attribute classes in different namespaces cause the metadata edge to be dropped as ambiguous). Both the `impact` ambiguity guard (`IsMetadataTargetUnambiguous`) and the `deps` ambiguity CTE (`target_ambiguity`) are additionally tightened to count class-like definitions at symbol-identity level instead of path level: `IsMetadataTargetUnambiguous` now uses `SELECT DISTINCT f.path, s.line, s.name` so two same-named class-like definitions in one source file (e.g. idiomatic C# `namespace A { class FooAttribute { } } namespace B { class FooAttribute { } }` in a single .cs file) register as ambiguous; `target_ambiguity` joins `target_files` back through `files` + `symbols` with `COUNT(*)` over class-like symbol rows so the same same-file duplicate case correctly drops the `[Foo]` metadata edge. Path-level counting previously treated these same-file duplicates as count=1 because `SELECT DISTINCT f.path` and `target_files` (grouped by `dst.path`) both collapse the two definitions into a single row, so `cdidx deps` and `cdidx impact` were confidently reporting an ambiguous short-name metadata reference as a definite dependency / blast-radius edge — contradicting the design intent that "ambiguity" includes duplicates in one file. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpAttributeAmbiguityCountsSameFileDuplicateClassDefinitions` and `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_MetadataBypassAmbiguityGuard_CountsSameFileDuplicateDefinitions` to pin the symbol-identity-level counting for both `deps` and `impact`. `IsMetadataTargetUnambiguous` is additionally tightened to wrap `--path` / `--exclude-path` parameters through `EscapeLikeQuery` and bind them as `%...%` patterns, matching the LIKE semantics used by the rest of the reader (search / references / deps etc.); without the wrap the in-scope class-like count would underflow to 1 even when two same-named attribute classes sit side-by-side in the requested CLI subtree such as `--path src/A/`, and the metadata bypass would falsely fire. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencyHints_MetadataBypassAmbiguityGuard_CliPathPatternEscaping_SuppressesWhenInScopeIsAmbiguous` to pin this. `CSharpNoArgAttributeRegex` is additionally widened to accept an optional generic-argument list after the attribute name (`(?:\s*<[^\n]+?>)?`) so generic no-arg attribute forms such as `[MyAudit<int>]`, `[assembly: MyAttr<string>]`, the multi-line `[\n MyAttr<int>\n]`, and nested-generic forms like `[MyAttr<Dictionary<string, int>>]` / `[MyOther<ValueTuple<int, List<string>>>]` are indexed as `attribute` references instead of falling through both `CallRegex` (requires `(`) and the old no-arg regex (which ended at `]` / `,` / EOL and therefore rejected `<int>` between the name and `]`). The inner generic segment now uses a non-greedy `[^\n]+?` so nested `>` tokens (e.g. the closing `>` of an inner `Dictionary<string, int>`) no longer terminate the match prematurely — the old `[^>\n]+` excluded `>` and therefore broke on the first inner `>`, dropping the reference row for nested-generic attribute usages. Without the widening those sites produced zero reference rows, so `deps` / `impact` / `references` / `inspect` / `analyze_symbol` all missed the dependency edge to the real `Foo<T>Attribute` class file. Added `ReferenceExtractorTests.Extract_CsharpGenericNoArgAttribute_ClassifiedAsAttribute`, `ReferenceExtractorTests.Extract_CsharpNestedGenericNoArgAttribute_ClassifiedAsAttribute`, `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpGenericNoArgAttribute_StillIndexedAndResolvesToAttributeClass`, `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpGenericNoArgAttribute_AssemblyTarget_IsIndexed`, and `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharpNestedGenericNoArgAttribute_ResolvesToAttributeClass` to pin the end-to-end behavior. Both the `impact` ambiguity guard (`IsMetadataTargetUnambiguous`) and the `deps` ambiguity path (`target_files` / `target_ambiguity`) are additionally tightened to treat a C# class as a valid `[Attr]` metadata target ONLY when its signature inherits from an `Attribute`-suffixed base class (`signature LIKE '%: %Attribute%'`). Plain `class MyAuditAttribute { }` without `: Attribute` inheritance is not a valid `[MyAudit]` target at compile time, so counting it as an ambiguity candidate would under-report the `impact` blast radius and suppress a real `deps` metadata edge when a same-named plain class coexists with the real attribute class. `target_files` now exposes a new `has_metadata_target_kind` MAX column that applies the same C# signature filter, and `metadata_raw_suppression` / `target_ambiguity` / the metadata clause in `edges` are all switched to `has_metadata_target_kind`; Java / Kotlin / Scala targets remain unaffected because their metadata markers cannot be captured with a single portable signature LIKE, so they keep the broader class-like candidate set. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharp_PlainClassWithAttributeSuffixName_DoesNotCountAsAmbiguity` to pin the `deps` path. Round-17 follow-up loosens the C# metadata-target signature filter from `'%: %Attribute%'` (requires the immediate base class to end in `Attribute`) to `'%: %'` (any inheritance clause qualifies) so indirect inheritance like `class MyAuditAttribute : BaseAudit` where `BaseAudit : Attribute` is also recognized as a valid `[MyAudit]` target; transitive base-type resolution is not available at SQL time, so the inheritance-clause check is the best portable approximation — non-attribute derivations are over-accepted, but an invalid `[MyFoo]` against a non-attribute class would fail to compile and therefore does not appear as a real reference. The shared `BuildCSharpMetadataTargetFilter` helper additionally degrades to `1 = 1` (the pre-metadata-eligibility behavior) when the `symbols.signature` column is missing on legacy / read-only DBs where `TryMigrateForRead` could not add it, so `deps` / `impact` queries return results instead of crashing with `no such column: s.signature`. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharp_IndirectAttributeInheritance_ResolvesAsMetadataTarget` to pin the indirect-inheritance path. Round-18 follow-up replaces the boolean `BuildCSharpMetadataTargetFilter` helper with a unified `BuildMetadataTargetKindExpr(fileAlias)` expression that narrows the metadata-target candidate kind per language: C# accepts only `kind = 'class'` with an inheritance clause (with the same legacy `1 = 1` fallback to class-only when `symbols.signature` is missing), JavaScript/TypeScript accept `class` / `struct` / `interface` / `function` (so function-decorator factories like `function sealed(target) { ... }` targeted by `@sealed` stay as valid `deps` edges), and other graph-supported languages keep the broader class/struct/interface candidate set. The old filter applied only the C# signature clause and left `s.kind IN ('class', 'struct', 'interface')` outside, which (a) wrongly counted `struct MyAuditAttribute` / `interface MyAuditAttribute` as C# metadata-target ambiguity candidates even though neither can derive from `System.Attribute`, and (b) dropped JS/TS decorator edges to a `function sealed` factory because `has_metadata_target_kind` required a class-like kind. The new expression is applied at three call sites: `IsMetadataTargetUnambiguous` (via a precomputed `metadataTargetKindExprF` local), the `target_files` CTE `has_metadata_target_kind` MAX column, and the `target_ambiguity` CTE JOIN condition (where the outer `s.kind IN (...)` narrowing is removed since the new expression already encodes the per-language kind rule). Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_JavaScriptFunctionDecorator_ResolvesAsDependency` (JS `@sealed` class → `function sealed(target)` factory file now produces a deps edge instead of being dropped) and `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharp_SameNameInterface_DoesNotBlockMetadataEdge` (same-named `interface MyAuditAttribute` no longer ambiguates `[MyAudit]` → `class MyAuditAttribute : Attribute`). Round-19 follow-up additionally tightens the C# clause to accept rows whose `signature` is NULL when the column itself exists (`s.signature IS NULL OR s.signature LIKE '%: %'`): the previous `s.signature IS NOT NULL AND s.signature LIKE '%: %'` rejected every row on a DB whose schema was migrated in place by `TryMigrateForRead` without reindexing (the column is added but existing rows keep NULL signatures), so real `[MyAudit]` → `class MyAuditAttribute : System.Attribute` edges silently disappeared from `deps` / `impact` until the user re-ran `cdidx index`. Matching the spirit of the column-missing `1 = 1` fallback, NULL signatures are now treated as eligible instead of being rejected outright. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharp_LegacyDbWithNullSignature_StillResolvesAttributeEdge` (NULL-signature attribute class still resolves the `deps` edge). Round-20 follow-up tightens the NULL-signature fallback to the canonical C# attribute naming convention (`name LIKE '%Attribute'`) instead of accepting every NULL-signature class, so a legacy-migration DB no longer counts arbitrary same-named non-attribute classes (`HelperClient : BaseService`) as metadata-target candidates that would silently inject false ambiguity against a real `[MyAudit]` → `MyAuditAttribute` edge. DBs without any `signature` column at all degrade to the same naming heuristic, and the existing `GetFileDependencies_CSharp_LegacyDbWithNullSignature_StillResolvesAttributeEdge` regression still passes because `MyAuditAttribute` ends with `Attribute` and therefore survives the tightened fallback. Round-20 also drops `interface` from the JavaScript / TypeScript metadata-target candidate kind set (`class` + `function` only): TypeScript `interface` is a compile-time type-only construct and cannot be a decorator target at runtime, so including it would let a same-named `interface` inject false ambiguity against a real `function` / `class` decorator provider and silently drop the `@sealed` → `function sealed(target)` deps edge. Added `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_CSharp_LegacyDbWithNullSignature_NonAttributeName_DoesNotBlockMetadataEdge` (arbitrary NULL-signature class with a non-`Attribute` name no longer injects false ambiguity) and `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_JavaScript_SameNameInterface_DoesNotBlockFunctionDecoratorEdge` (same-name `interface sealed` does not suppress the `@sealed` → `function sealed(target)` deps edge). The remaining edge case — a non-attribute class that already follows the `Attribute` naming convention or has an unrelated `: ` inheritance clause silently suppressing the real edge — is tracked as #435 and requires a schema-level `is_metadata_target` column to resolve cleanly, so it is deliberately deferred out of this PR to keep the #293 scope focused on the already-landed attribute / annotation classification work. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Database/DbReader.cs`, `src/CodeIndex/Indexer/ReferenceExtractor.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/DbReaderTests.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/ReferenceExtractorTests.cs`.
- **MCP `callers` / `callees` `kind` schema, CLI help, and README `--kind` option row no longer advertise metadata kinds as valid filter values (#293 follow-up)** — The `callers` / `callees` handlers reject `kind: "attribute"` / `kind: "annotation"` with a usage error (CLI) / `isError` tool response (MCP), but the MCP tool schema's `kind` property description still listed all five kinds as if they were valid filter values (`"Filter by reference kind (call, instantiate, subscribe, attribute, annotation)"`), `cdidx --help` similarly lumped `callers` / `callees` together with `references` for the `--kind` help row, and the README `--kind` option table (EN line 436 / JP line 1307) still directed readers to pass `--kind attribute` or `--kind annotation` on `callers` / `callees`. Schema and handler now agree: the `callers` / `callees` `kind` description now reads `"Filter by call-graph reference kind (call, instantiate, subscribe). Metadata kinds (attribute, annotation) are rejected here; use \`references\` for metadata enumeration."`, the CLI `--kind` help row splits `references` (accepts all five kinds) from `callers` / `callees` (call-graph kinds only, metadata rejected, redirects to `references`), and the README `--kind` row (both English and Japanese) now explicitly states that `callers` / `callees` reject `--kind attribute|annotation` with a usage error and points to `references --kind attribute|annotation` as the correct metadata-enumeration path. The MCP `references` tool description is unchanged because it still accepts every indexed kind. Added `McpServerTests.ToolsList_CallersCalleesKindDescription_ExcludesMetadataKinds` to pin the corrected schema wording. Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Mcp/McpToolDefinitions.cs`, `src/CodeIndex/Cli/ConsoleUi.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/McpServerTests.cs`, `README.md`.
- **`deps`, `impact`, `references`, `inspect`, and `analyze_symbol` retain metadata references as compile-time dependency edges and canonicalize the C# attribute-suffix convention (#293 follow-up)** — `DbReader.GetFileDependencies` (backing `cdidx deps`) and `DbReader.GetFileDependencyHintsToResolvedType` (backing `cdidx impact` / MCP `impact_analysis` heuristic file-hint fallback) keep metadata references in their logical reference CTE. Renaming or removing an attribute class still breaks annotated sites such as `[JsonConverterAttribute]` at compile time, so file-level blast-radius analysis must surface those edges as real dependencies — now labeled `attribute` / `annotation` in `logical_reference_kind` (previously these same sites leaked in as phantom `call` rows before classification was corrected). `GetFileDependencies` additionally canonicalizes the C# attribute naming convention: idiomatic `[Foo]` usage is stored with `symbol_name = "Foo"` but the defining class is `FooAttribute`, so the logical-reference CTE now UNION-ALLs a suffix-aliased copy of every C# `attribute`-kind row with `'Attribute'` appended (only when the original symbol_name does not already end in `Attribute`) so the target-file join reaches the attribute class file. `GetFileDependencyHintsToResolvedType` also aggregates a per-candidate `has_metadata_ref` flag and bypasses the `SourceFileHasStructuredTypeEvidence` guard for edges whose contributing references are purely metadata, so pure-attribute consumer files such as `[MyAudit] class Svc` now surface through `impact MyAuditAttribute` instead of being filtered out. `ResolveImpactFallbackNames` symmetrically adds suffix-stripped aliases for C# class names ending in `Attribute`, so the BFS-less file-hint path can find `[Foo]` sites whose source symbol_name does not match the defining class name. The same canonicalization is propagated to the symbol-level reference reader: `DbReader.SearchReferences`, `CountSearchReferences`, and `CountSearchReferencesTotal` (backing `references`, `inspect`, MCP `analyze_symbol`) now compute a C#-only `queryAttributeAlias` (defined in the new `ComputeCSharpAttributeSuffixAlias` helper) and OR it into both exact (folded and NOCASE) and substring WHERE clauses, so `references MyAuditAttribute` (and `inspect MyAuditAttribute` / `analyze_symbol MyAuditAttribute`) surface the idiomatic `[MyAudit]` call site consistently with `deps` / `impact`. Substring mode uses an exact-OR for the alias (not a second LIKE) so user queries like `MyAuditAttribute` do not over-match unrelated names such as `FooAuditLog`. The alias is C# only, so Java / Kotlin / Scala / TypeScript annotation sites remain unaffected. `callers` / `callees` intentionally skip the alias because they filter to the shared call-graph kinds (`call`, `instantiate`, `subscribe`) and reject `--kind attribute|annotation` at the CLI / MCP boundary — those commands model the dynamic call graph, not the dependency graph. The alias branch is additionally scoped so it cannot produce false positives: `ComputeCSharpAttributeSuffixAlias` returns `null` when `referenceKind` is a non-`attribute` call-graph kind (so `references FooAttribute --kind call` stays strict and does not match `Foo()`), and the SQL alias disjunct in all three reader methods is clamped to `f.lang = 'csharp' AND r.reference_kind = 'attribute'` so an unscoped `references FooAttribute` (no `--lang` / no `--kind`) still cannot bleed into Java annotations or C# call rows. Suffix detection is also case-insensitive (`OrdinalIgnoreCase`) so `references myauditattribute` and `inspect MyAuditATTRIBUTE` still produce the `MyAudit` alias, consistent with the NOCASE / folded contract of the surrounding exact / substring query paths. Added regression coverage `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_IncludesMetadataReferencesAsCompileTimeDependencies` (runtime + metadata edges both surface), `DbReaderTests.GetFileDependencies_MatchesCSharpAttributeSuffixConvention` (`[MyAudit]` → `MyAuditAttribute` canonicalization through `deps`), `DbReaderTests.SearchReferences_MatchesCSharpAttributeSuffixConvention_Substring` / `_Exact` / `_CSharpAttributeSuffixAliasDoesNotBleedToOtherLanguages` (same canonicalization through `references` / `inspect` / `analyze_symbol`, plus C#-only scope guard), `DbReaderTests.SearchReferences_CSharpAttributeSuffixAlias_NotAppliedToCallKind` (alias must not fire under `--kind call`), `DbReaderTests.SearchReferences_CSharpAttributeSuffixAlias_UnscopedLangStillLimitsToCSharpAttributeRows` (unscoped query must not match Java annotations or C# call rows), and `DbReaderTests.SearchReferences_CSharpAttributeSuffixAlias_CaseInsensitiveQuery` (lowercase / mixed-case queries still produce the alias). Affected: `src/CodeIndex/Database/DbReader.cs`, `tests/CodeIndex.Tests/DbReaderTests.cs`.
- **`callers` / `callees` now reject `--kind attribute|annotation` at the CLI and MCP boundary, and Swift / Gradle `@` metadata is reclassified as `annotation` (#293 follow-up)** — Metadata rows (`attribute` / `annotation`) are attributed to their enclosing body-range symbol rather than the annotated target, so `callers Obsolete --kind attribute` would silently return `[Obsolete] void M()` under the enclosing class (not `M`), and file-level targets such as `[assembly: CLSCompliant]` or Kotlin `@file:JvmName` would drop entirely because `container_name` is `NULL`. `QueryCommandRunner.RunCallers` / `RunCallees` now reject `--kind attribute` and `--kind annotation` with `CommandExitCodes.UsageError`, and the MCP `callers` / `callees` tools return an `isError` tool response; both paths direct users to `references <name> --kind attribute|annotation`, which IS a correct metadata enumeration path. Separately, `AnnotationLanguages` now includes `swift` and `gradle`, so Swift `@available(iOS 13.0, *)` / `@objc` / `@MainActor` and Gradle/Groovy `@CompileStatic` / `@TaskAction` are recorded as `annotation` instead of `call` (previously the `@Name(args)` forms leaked into `callers` / `callees` / `hotspots` / `impact` as phantom call edges, and the no-arg `@objc` / `@MainActor` / `@CompileStatic` / `@TaskAction` forms dropped from the index entirely because no-arg annotation emission was gated to languages in this set).
